_meta.description: FraudGuard legal and compliance rules engine configuration. Based on Kenya POCAMLA 2009 (Revised 2023) and POCAMLA Regulations 2023.

legal_rules.rule_name: Cash Transaction Report — Mandatory Regulatory Threshold
legal_rules.act_name: Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023
legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This transaction meets the mandatory cash transaction reporting threshold under Regulation 40 of the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023 because the cash amount of {amount} {currency} (equivalent to USD {usd_equivalent}) equals or exceeds the mandatory reporting threshold of USD 15,000. This report is mandatory regardless of whether the transaction appears suspicious.
legal_rules.description: Reporting institutions must file reports with the Centre on all cash transactions equivalent to or exceeding USD 15,000 or its equivalent in any other currency, whether or not the transaction appears suspicious.

legal_rules.rule_name: Cross-Border Monetary Instrument Declaration — Mandatory Declaration Threshold
legal_rules.act_name: Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023
legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This case meets the cross-border declaration threshold under Regulation 10 of the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023 because the amount conveyed ({amount} {currency}, equivalent to USD {usd_equivalent}) equals or exceeds the mandatory declaration threshold of USD 10,000. Cross-border conveyance of monetary instruments at or above this value must be declared to customs and reported to the Centre under Section 12 of the POCAMLA Act.
legal_rules.description: Any person intending to convey into or out of Kenya monetary instruments equivalent to or exceeding USD 10,000 must declare the particulars to a customs officer. Reporting institutions must file with the Centre.

legal_rules.rule_name: Suspicious Transaction / Activity Report — ML-Detected High Risk
legal_rules.section_or_regulation: Section 44 of the Act; Regulation 38 of the 2023 Regulations
legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This transaction has been flagged as a suspicious activity report candidate under Section 44 of the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Act (Revised 2023) and Regulation 38 of the 2023 Regulations. The ML anomaly model assigned a fraud probability of {ml_score_pct}%, which meets the threshold for suspicious activity reporting. Reporting institutions must report to the Centre within two days of suspicion arising, with sufficient supporting information. This auto-submission satisfies that two-day obligation.
legal_rules.description: Reporting institutions must monitor complex, unusual, suspicious, large, and unusual-pattern transactions. Where suspicion of ML/TF/PF arises, the institution must report to the Centre within two days.

legal_rules.rule_name: Source of Funds Escalation — Large, Frequent, or Unusual Transactions
legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This transaction has been identified as requiring source-of-funds assessment under Regulation 37 of the Proceeds of Crime and Anti-Money Laundering Regulations, 2023. The transaction characteristics — including {pattern_flags} — indicate a large, frequent, or unusual cash transaction requiring the reporting institution to assess the legitimacy of the source of funds and the purpose of the transaction before proceeding. This case is referred for analyst review.
legal_rules.description: For large, frequent, or unusual cash deposits, withdrawals, transfers, exchanges, foreign transactions, or related patterns, the institution must assess the legitimacy of source of funds and transaction purpose.

legal_rules.act_name: Institution Compliance Policy / FRC Operational Guidance
legal_rules.section_or_regulation: Institution Compliance Policy; POCAMLA Act Section 44 (monitoring obligations)
legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This transaction exceeded the configured institutional/FRC critical threshold of KES 1,950,000 (transaction amount: KES {kes_amount}) and has been escalated under the institution's compliance policy framework together with POCAMLA suspicious transaction monitoring obligations under Section 44 of the POCAMLA Act. Note: The KES 1,950,000 threshold is an institutional/FRC operational policy trigger and not an independently stated statutory threshold under POCAMLA. However, all transactions at this level are subject to the broad transaction monitoring duties imposed by Section 44 and Regulation 38.
legal_rules.description: Configurable institutional policy threshold. Transactions at or above KES 1,950,000 are treated as critical compliance triggers requiring immediate escalation and FRC notification. This threshold is policy-based, not statutory, but is paired with POCAMLA monitoring obligations.

legal_rules.rule_name: Full Balance Depletion Pattern — Suspicious Activity Indicator
legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This transaction triggered a full account balance depletion pattern — a key indicator of possible money laundering or fraudulent fund movement — under the transaction monitoring obligations of Section 44(1) of the POCAMLA Act (Revised 2023). The source account balance was reduced to zero following this {tx_type} transaction of {amount} {currency}, which is consistent with patterns associated with layering or flight of funds.
legal_rules.description: Full source account balance depletion in a single TRANSFER or CASH_OUT is a recognised suspicious pattern under POCAMLA monitoring obligations.

legal_rules.legal_reason_template: This transaction involved a destination account with a zero prior balance receiving funds of {amount} {currency}, which is a recognised indicator of possible structuring, mule account activity, or layering under Section 44(1) monitoring obligations of the POCAMLA Act (Revised 2023). This case has been flagged for analyst review.
legal_rules.description: Destination account with zero prior balance receiving significant funds is a suspicious pattern requiring monitoring under Section 44.
